At dawn, checks for pet arrivals
This page helps new colleagues see what to do first

Companion Animal Travel Desk arrival handling matters because early checks prevent avoidable stress, delay, and error. You must read each booking note before you approach the crate, then confirm the animal, the carrier, and the destination against the record. Speak softly, move with purpose, and keep the area clear so the pet remains calm.

When a traveler presents a rabbit, inspect the crate for secure latches, clean bedding, and enough room for safe posture. <<FACT F064>> Record any concern at once, then ask the senior coordinator to review the case before acceptance. If a crate shows damage, do not improvise a repair; use approved equipment and follow the humane handling method.

For cats, check ventilation, floor space, and label visibility before transfer. <<FACT F067>> Watch for signs of distress such as heavy panting, hiding, or resistance, and report them promptly. The cabin team relies on accurate handover notes, so write clearly and note feeding, water, and comfort needs exactly as observed.

If a pet travels with a care plan, read it in full and match your actions to the species, temperament, and comfort guidance. Keep the owner informed in plain language, but never promise an outcome you cannot confirm. Leila Okafor and Marcus Fischer may ask for reassurance, yet the desk must stay focused on procedure and safe handling.

Remember that calm, humane action and clear records protect the animal, the traveler, and the airline.
